title: Manchester City’s Erling Haaland invests in new chess tournament with $2.7m prize pot
content:
Manchester City striker Erling Haaland has invested in a new world chess championship.

The 25-year-old has co-founded the company Chess Mate, which has become a “significant” owner in Norway Chess, the organisation behind the newly-launched event, the Total Chess World Championship Tour.

Haaland drew similarities between chess and the tactical and mental side of football, and said his decision to invest was motivated by a desire to make chess a “bigger spectator sport globally”. The Norway international was wearing a Norway Chess cap as he walked from the Manchester City coach through the London Stadium before Saturday’s Premier League fixture against West Ham United.

The Total Chess World Championship Tour will consist of four tournaments a year and will feature a $2.7million (£2.3m) prize pot, a press release from Norway Chess confirmed.

“Chess is a fantastic game,” Haaland said in a press release. “It sharpens the brain and has many similarities to football. You have to think quickly, trust your instincts, and think many moves ahead. Strategy and planning are absolutely crucial.”

The new tournament and format is approved by the International Chess Federation (FIDE), the sport’s international governing body, and players will compete across three disciplines — Fast Classic, Rapid and Blitz — to crown the FIDE Combined World Champion and “the most complete and versatile chess player in the world”.

A pilot tournament is planned for the autumn of 2026 before a full championship season in 2027.

Chess world No 1, and the sport’s most high-profile player, Magnus Carlsen, is also Norwegian and speaking to chess media outlet Take, Take, Take in January, he said Haaland was the footballer he would most like to be compared to.

Haaland has co-founded Chess Mate alongside Norwegian entrepreneur Morten Borge.

A number of top football players and managers have spoken about their interest in chess. In May, Arsenal’s Eberechi Eze won $20,000 in an online celebrity chess tournament — he told The Athletic in a 2023 interview that his former Crystal Palace team-mate Michael Olise, now at Bayern Munich, had taught him how to play.

England internationals Harry Kanes, Trent Alexander-Arnold, and Anthony Gordon have also spoken about their love of playing chess, as has Liverpool forward Mohamed Salah. Former Chelsea head coach Enzo Maresca wrote a 7,000-word thesis on the parallels between football and chess, while Manchester City head coach Pep Guardiola has spoken about studying the methods of Carlsen.

“Chess – like football – has always been a global language of strategy and creativity,” FIDE president Arkady Dvorkovich added. “Seeing a world-class athlete like Erling Haaland join the Total World Chess Championship Tour is a powerful signal of the global attention and cultural relevance that chess enjoys today.”
